title: Augmented strict quotient pullback comparison for a Cartesian open square
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R$, a uniformizer $t$, and $A_n=R/t^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $U'\xrightarrow a U$, $j':U'\hookrightarrow X'$, $j:U\hookrightarrow X$, $h:X'\to X$ be a Cartesian open square of finite-type $k$-schemes [def-cbc-open-immersion-square, def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. On their small pro-etale sites put $B_W=\lim_n(A_n)_W$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients] and use ordinary unbounded derived module categories $D(B_W)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Restriction is exact ringed-slice restriction [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact]. The structural maps $g^{-1}B_W\to B_V$ for $g:V\to W$ are induced by the constant-section maps at all quotient projections, as in [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback].
Let $H\in D(B_X)$ be derived complete [def-weil-derived-complete]. Choose a flat-term K-flat complex $P$ representing $H$ [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules, lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Write $Q_W(H)_n=\operatorname{Res}_n(H\otimes^L_{B_W}(A_n)_W)$ with its strict quotient transitions [def-weil-integral-reduction-tower]. For $g:V\to W$, let $F_gQ_W(H)$ denote simultaneous finite constant-coefficient pullback of this tower, regarded over $B_V$ through its quotient projections. Let $V_h(P)$ and $V_a(j^*P)$ be the strict tower complexes with terms $h_n^*(P\otimes_{B_X}(A_n)_X)$ and $a_n^*(j^*P\otimes_{B_U}(A_n)_U)$, respectively. Let $\gamma_h:\Delta h^*P\to V_h(P)$ and $\gamma_a:\Delta a^*j^*P\to V_a(j^*P)$ be the actual pulled quotient augmentations, induced by $p\mapsto p\otimes1$. Write $\delta_P:j'^*h^*P\xrightarrow{\sim}a^*j^*P$ for ordinary ringed-square composition in its section normalization [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization].
The finite compositors and restriction/quotient comparisons specify a natural strict tower isomorphism
$$\alpha_P:j'^*V_h(P)\xrightarrow{\sim}V_a(j^*P),\qquad \alpha_P\,j'^*\gamma_h=\gamma_a\,\Delta(\delta_P).$$
The augmentation equality holds on complexes of simultaneous strict towers: on every balanced local tensor $r'\otimes p$, both augmented maps have value $r'_n\otimes(p\otimes1)$ at $n$, with the original differentials and all quotient transitions. The structural maps used after restriction and after composition agree as maps into $B_{U'}$, with identical $n$th projections. These identifications descend naturally and independently of $P$ to a specified isomorphism $\alpha_H:j'^*F_hQ_X(H)\xrightarrow{\sim}F_aQ_U(j^*H)$ in the derived category of strict towers.
Write $L_W=R\lim$ and let $\rho_T:j'^*L_{X'}T\xrightarrow{\sim}L_{U'}j'^*T$ be the normalized exact-product comparison [lem-cbc-exact-product-functor-strict-limit]. Define $c_H=L_{U'}(\alpha_H)\rho_{F_hQ_X(H)}$. This is a natural isomorphism $j'^*Lh^*_{\mathrm{comp}}H\xrightarrow{\sim}La^*_{\mathrm{comp}}j^*H$. For the actual ordinary-to-completed units $v_h,v_a$ induced by $\gamma_h,\gamma_a$ [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback, def-sf-pull-completion-comparison], and the derived ordinary compositor $\delta_H$, it satisfies
$$c_H\,j'^*v_h=v_a\,\delta_H.$$
The equality uses the same strict augmentations under the normalized Roos maps, with product component $\gamma$ and zero shifted component. It is preserved by the counit-normalized coefficient and representative identifications of [lem-cbc-adic-pullback-presentation-transport]. No invertibility of $h^{-1}B_X\to B_{X'}$ or faithfulness of separate derived evaluations is assumed.

source.place: Tag 099N, lemma-pushforward-Noetherian-case (2),(5); sites-cohomology.tex Tag 0D6D, lemma-derived-pullback-composition, and Tag 0941, lemma-derived-limit-is-ok. Agent-formulated strict augmented square extracted from old steps 8 and 9 of lem-sf-open-exchange-roos-restriction.

proof.text: First identify the ringed square, before deriving anything. Restriction is the right adjoint of exact open extension, so it preserves inverse limits. Consequently $j^*B_X=B_U$ and $j'^*B_{X'}=B_{U'}$, with their specified quotient projections. The finite constant-ring structural maps are the constant-section isomorphisms. At each $n$, their composites around the square send a constant $a\in A_n$ to that same constant $a$; by the sheafification defining the constant sheaves these are equal ring-sheaf maps. Hence both maps from the common inverse image of $B_X$ to $B_{U'}$ have $n$th component the inverse image of $\pi_{X,n}$ followed by this same finite constant map. The universal property of $B_{U'}=\lim_n(A_n)_{U'}$ makes the completed structural maps equal. Apply the structural-map assertion of the presentation-transport lemma to these two constructions. This proves equality of the completed maps themselves, not an assertion that inverse image preserves that completed limit.

source.place: Tag 0D6D, lemma-derived-pullback-composition; agent calculation of the strict quotient square on flat-term K-flat models.

proof.text: Choose $P$ as in the statement using the K-flat resolution lemma. Restriction $j^*P$ and each ordinary ringed pullback of $P$ are K-flat with flat terms by preservation under ringed pullback; no flatness of the structural ring maps is needed. Thus $P_n=P\otimes_{B_X}(A_n)_X$ computes the derived reduction, with transitions $1\otimes q_{m,n}$ and augmentation $p\mapsto p\otimes1$. Finite constant-coefficient pullback is exact, so $h_n^*P_n$ and $a_n^*((j^*P)_n)$ compute the two finite pulled towers. The restriction/reduction comparison identifies $j^*P_n$ with $(j^*P)\otimes_{B_U}(A_n)_U$ by the ordinary tensor comparison and includes the quotient units and all transitions. Its hypotheses hold because open restriction has the ring identification of step 1. Also $j^*H$ is complete by open restriction of quotient-tower completeness. Both completeness statements are in the Roos-triangle sense, whereas completed pullback is defined on derived $I$-complete objects in the intrinsic Koszul sense. Since $\ell$ is invertible on $X$ and $U$, the pair $(R,(t))$ satisfies the adic coefficient datum and $B_W$ is the completed sheaf $A_W$ of that datum, by [lem-sf-open-quotient-koszul-completeness]. The Roos/intrinsic completeness equivalence (i)$\Leftrightarrow$(iv) then makes $H$ and $j^*H$ derived $I$-complete in the intrinsic sense [lem-pur-roos-intrinsic-completeness-equivalence]. Therefore both completed pullbacks in the conclusion have their stated domains.

source.place: Tag 0D6D, lemma-derived-pullback-composition; agent calculation of the strict quotient square on flat-term K-flat models.

proof.text:
For each $n$ apply the section-normalized open-square compositor at the finite constant ring $A_n$ to $P_n$, and then apply $a_n^*$ to the restriction/reduction comparison of step 2. This gives
$$\alpha_{P,n}:j'^*h_n^*P_n\longrightarrow a_n^*((j^*P)_n).$$
Both factors are isomorphisms. Their naturality in the coefficient quotient and in $P$ implies compatibility with $1\otimes q_{m,n}$; equivalently, on a local inverse-image tensor generator they preserve the coefficient and the section, and a quotient replaces the coefficient by its image under $q_{m,n}$ on either route. They commute with $d_P$, since the coefficient rings have degree zero and these are degree-preserving module comparisons. Thus the components and their inverses define one natural chain isomorphism $\alpha_P$ of strict towers. Here the normalized finite compositor is evaluated on actual complexes; it is not an inference that a family of equalities in separate derived evaluations determines a tower map.

source.place: Tag 0D6D, lemma-derived-pullback-composition; agent calculation of the strict quotient square on flat-term K-flat models.

proof.text: Check the augmentation on the same chain models. After the ordinary open-square tensor identification, a homogeneous local generator of $j'^*h^*P$ is $r'\otimes p$. The left route first takes its quotient augmentation to $r'_n\otimes(p\otimes1)$ and then applies the finite compositor; the right route first applies $\delta_P$, retaining $r'$ and $p$, and then takes that same quotient augmentation. Hence both routes give $r'_n\otimes(p\otimes1)$. This is an equality of balanced tensor maps: multiplying $p$ by $b$ is multiplication by the common image of $b$ in $(A_n)_{U'}$, by step 1. Bilinearity extends it to the presheaf tensors, and functoriality of their sheafification gives equality of the sheaf maps. The differential sends the displayed value to $r'_n\otimes(dp\otimes1)$; a quotient transition sends it to $r'_m\otimes(p\otimes1)$ at level $m\le n$. Therefore $\alpha_Pj'^*\gamma_h=\gamma_a\Delta(\delta_P)$ as strict augmented chain maps.

source.place: Tag 0D6D, lemma-derived-pullback-composition; agent calculation of the strict quotient square on flat-term K-flat models.

proof.text: Now descend the actual tower comparison. If $P\to P'$ is a quasi-isomorphism between good representatives, derived change of rings makes $P_n\to P'_n$ a quasi-isomorphism for every $n$; exact finite pullback and exact restriction preserve these maps. Kernels and cokernels of strict towers are computed levelwise, so the resulting strict tower map is a quasi-isomorphism. The good-representative localization is an equivalence by the site derived-tensor descent lemma. Its localization universal property therefore descends $\alpha_P$, its inverse, and its naturality to a specified natural isomorphism $\alpha_H$ between the two functors to the derived category of strict towers. The same reasoning descends the augmentation equality of step 4. In particular a roof between representatives gives the same conjugated comparison after its quasi-isomorphisms are inverted. This proves independence of $P$ for the entire augmented diagram, not merely for its finite derived evaluations.

source.place: Tag 0D6D, lemma-derived-pullback-composition; agent calculation of the strict quotient square on flat-term K-flat models.

proof.text: The exact-product strict-limit comparison applies to $F=j'^*$. Indeed $j'^*$ is exact and is a right adjoint, hence preserves countable products with the projection-characterized comparison. Countable products of module sheaves over both small pro-etale sites are exact, for the completed coefficient rings as well. Let $T=F_hQ_X(H)$. The cited comparison gives the normalized isomorphism $\rho_T:j'^*L_{X'}T\to L_{U'}j'^*T$. Applying the functor $L_{U'}$ to $\alpha_H$ and composing gives $c_H=L_{U'}(\alpha_H)\rho_T$. Both factors are natural isomorphisms. By the definition of completed pullback its source and target are respectively $j'^*Lh^*_{\mathrm{comp}}H$ and $La^*_{\mathrm{comp}}j^*H$.

source.place: Tag 099N, lemma-pushforward-Noetherian-case (2),(5); sites-cohomology.tex Tag 0941, lemma-derived-limit-is-ok; normalized comparison is the cited exact-product lemma.

proof.text:
Let $u(\gamma)$ denote the canonical map from the source of a strict augmentation to its total derived limit. The augmentation clause of the exact-product comparison gives $\rho_Tj'^*u(\gamma_h)=u(j'^*\gamma_h)$. Naturality of the constant-tower/derived-limit unit and the chain equality in step 4 give
$$L(\alpha_H)u(j'^*\gamma_h)=u(\gamma_a)\delta_H.$$
The actual maps $v_h,v_a$ are these $u(\gamma_h),u(\gamma_a)$ by the quotient-augmentation definition of completed pullback. Combining the two displayed equalities proves $c_Hj'^*v_h=v_a\delta_H$. More explicitly, in the normalized Roos complex of a strict tower, $u(\gamma)$ has coordinates $((\gamma_n)_n,0)$. The product map of restriction and the tower map $\alpha_P$ act on both signed summands; the second coordinate stays zero and the first becomes the common generator formula of step 4. This checks the asserted normalization on chain maps, including the original differentials, rather than choosing a map of cones in a triangulated category.

source.place: Tag 0941, lemma-derived-limit-is-ok; agent augmentation computation using the cited normalized exact-product comparison.

proof.text: Finally compare coefficient presentations and resolving choices using the presentation-transport lemma. Step 1 verifies its required equality of all quotient projections; our ordinary comparisons are the identity on the same balanced generators. On good representatives its prescribed derived identifications are characterized by the universal counit equations, so they carry these tower maps and their constant-tower augmentations to the ones just used. The lemma states $E_Ku_1=u_2e_K$, including the strict quotient transitions and finite-reduction identifications. Conjugate the equality of step 7 by these comparisons on its source and target; the middle comparison and its inverse cancel, yielding the same unit equation in the transported presentation. Thus the result retains the actual units under the stipulated coefficient and representative identifications. The argument used equality into the completed ring by its projections and equality of strict augmented chain maps; it never required the structural ring map to be invertible or separate derived evaluations to be faithful.
